children: U.S. subsidiaries have reached an agreement with Amtrak to resolve a decade-long dispute between the two over passenger service delays, equipment issues, and late station departures.

is the parent company of U.S. rail subsidiaries Illinois Central Railroad Company and Grand Trunk Western Railroad Company. Amtrak runs passenger trains on U.S. rail lines owned by CNI U.S. subsidiaries for several intercity routes, including the City of New Orleans (between Chicago and New Orleans), Illini and Saluki (between Chicago and Carbondale, Illinois), and Wolverine (between Chicago and Pontiac, Michigan).

The dispute involves delays Amtrak blames on CNI for prioritizing freight routes over passenger routes, while CNI blames Amtrak for freight delays due to Amtrak equipment issues or late station departures.

Accordingly, CNI has pushed proposals to the Surface Transportation Board (STB) that would hold Amtrak financially responsible for delays, while Amtrak blames delays on the lack of Onboard Shunt Enhancers (OSEs) which detect trains at rail grade crossings. By equipping Amtrak trains with OSEs, both freight and passenger trains would move more efficiently across corridors Amtrak shares with CNI.

As part of their eight-year operating agreement, Amtrak and CNI have agreed to a revised performance payment system that is more closely aligned to the Federal Railroad Administration’s on-time performance standard, regular reviews of Amtrak’s schedules, and a process to address operational issues and resolve disputes.
The two will also work together to equip Amtrak trains with OSEs.

“[Canadian National] is pleased to have reached agreements that allow us to move forward with a clear framework for safely and efficiently sharing our network. Together with the deployment of OSE technology, these agreements will support safer grade crossings and reliable passenger and freight service,” said Canadian National COO Patrick Whitehead.
Although the agreement ends a decade-long dispute between the two sides, Canadian National
shares are lower as the negotiations highlight the railroad’s persistent on-time performance challenges.

title: Canadian National, Amtrak back on track, ending 10-year-long dispute over delays
